user_stories.i_want_to: enter inventory consumption details, select correction or damage mode, look up container and product codes, specify quantities, and commit the adjustment in a single atomic transaction
user_stories.so_that: I can accurately adjust stock levels for damaged goods or correct entry details in one seamless operation, ensuring data integrity across all related inventory tables

acceptance_criteria.given: the consumption record entry screen is open with valid source rows and the user has selected correction mode, filled in all required fields (product code, container code, consumption quantity, count, deposit date, expiry date), and all validations pass

acceptance_criteria.then: the system presents a diff summary for confirmation, acquires a database lock, executes the multi‑table transaction, shows a success message, and closes the window with an update success flag returned to the parent screen

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has entered a consumption count (kosu) that exceeds the available stock count (sosu) for a selected source row
acceptance_criteria.when: the user changes the value in the count field and moves the focus away
acceptance_criteria.then: an error message 'Entered count exceeds available stock' is displayed and the invalid value is rejected, preventing the record from being saved until corrected

acceptance_criteria.given: exactly one source row was selected on the parent screen before opening the entry window
acceptance_criteria.when: the consumption record entry screen opens
acceptance_criteria.then: the correction form is pre‑populated with the product code, lot number, container code, dates, AM/PM value, and quantities from that single row, allowing the operator to make minor corrections without re‑typing

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: PowerBuilder modal response window w_keijyo_appropriate_ken (datawindow dw_keijyo bound to dw_keijyo_appropriate_ken, shared source grid dw_data bound to dw_keijyo_ken). Update button cb_update.clicked fully overrides ancestor flow; calls fw_ck_dwchange, u_updtchek, fw_make_upmes, fw_table_lock, then embedded SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE across M_ZAIKOKJ, M_DEVZAIKO, M_DEVZAIKOIO, M_ZAILOTEDA, M_SYOHINNAIYO under manual transaction FATRA with explicit f_commit/f_rollback. Quantity‑count auto‑calc on dw_data::u_post_itemchange (Ceiling(suryo/nisnaiyo)). Product/container lookup via embedded SQL in dw_keijyo::u_post_itemchange and popup w_pub_pop_nisyoucd. Pre‑fill on open when dw_data.RowCount()=1. Close button cb_close.clicked resets viewflg, calls ShareDataOff, and returns b_upflg via CloseWithReturn.
user_stories.migration_hint: Implement as POST /api/v1/research-stock/corrections with a single @Transactional service method. Request body includes correctionType (CORRECT/DAMAGE), header (correctedNyukoydt, correctedAjikokukbn, correctedZaiyukou, correctedKosuu, correctedNisyoucd, memo, azukesokocd, paletno), and source rows with enteredQty and pieceCount overrides. Server‑side: validate required dates (not 0000/00/00, zaiyukou ≥ nyukoydt), quantity/count bounds, mixed‑warehouse check; use pessimistic table lock (PostgreSQL advisory lock) on relevant tables; execute the DML cascade in the exact order documented (header M_ZAIKOKJ INSERT, new M_DEVZAIKO inserts, M_ZAILOTEDA upsert, M_SYOHINNAIYO conditional insert, then per‑source‑row consumption loop with SELECT…ROWNUM=1 replacement using FETCH FIRST, M_ZAIKOKJ usage INSERT, and M_DEVZAIKO DELETE or UPDATE); commit only on full success. Pre‑fill and field lookup endpoints (GET /api/v1/products/{code}, GET /api/v1/containers/{code}) should be separate reusable services. Replace pb‑style string concatenation with parameterised queries.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All consumption record adjustments must execute within an atomic database transaction with full rollback on any step failure (mirroring the FATRA transaction scope).

Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on M_DEVZAIKO, M_ZAIKOKJ, and M_DEVZAIKOIO must persist an audit trail (mirroring f_ins_m_devzaikoio with g_KURO/g_AKA color codes) including user identity, timestamp, and before/after quantities.
